analysis.title: What Matters Today: We expect EPS growth of 27% in Q3, Le Penn's Hawkish Fiscal Package, Nuclear Stocks Rallying
key_insights: Goldman expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% in Q3 2026. The season starts the week of October 12. Consensus growth for Q3 is the highest heading into any reporting season since 2021, but it still implies a slowdown from the 33% realized in Q2, even excluding the other income from appreciating equity stakes last quarter.

Earnings growth is concentrated. Info Tech and Energy together are expected to contribute nearly 80% of Q3 growth. The top 10 contributing stocks are expected to account for over two-thirds, and Micron and Nvidia together for more than one third of index growth.
Most S&P 500 companies are expected to report continued profit margin strength in Q3, but input cost pressures likely limited substantial sequential margin expansion.

Consensus has hyperscaler capex growing 116% y/y in Q3 2026, versus 87% growth in Q2. Goldman expects 2027 hyperscaler capex to grow more than 50%, above the consensus of roughly $1.1 trillion. Signs of AI capex monetization matter for both the hyperscalers and the capex growth outlook.

Le Pen's first fiscal counter-proposals point to sharp deficit reduction, with the deficit cut to 3.7% of economic output in 2027 and 2.2% by 2032, mostly through spending cuts. OAT-Bund spreads are about 10bps lower this morning, helped by lower oil prices. French domestic equities and French banks are up about 2 standard deviations from depressed levels.

Goldman stays cautious on France until the budget details arrive in the coming weeks. It expects budget discussions and election noise to limit the government's ability to show tangible fiscal consolidation, so risk asymmetry could turn negative again. It also sees limited influence for Le Pen if elected. The author has a bearish bias and sees wait-and-see mode, and finds today's relief smaller than expected, so unsure it is enough to reengage on the sell side.

Nuclear stocks had three positive headlines in a week: $120bn for nuclear reactors in the U.S.-Korea strategic investment, a $4 billion U.S. loan offer for Vistra to boost nuclear output, and a 20-year Alphabet deal to buy 890 megawatts of new nuclear power from Constellation Energy.
Positioning in Goldman's Uranium basket (GSXURANI) is at the lows, and the desk asks whether it is time to reengage (attributed to Cullen Morgan).

A PJM ruling expected October 12 could require new data center loads of 50 MW or more entering service after June 1, 2027 to secure their own new capacity (Bring Your Own New Capacity) to avoid priority curtailment. Goldman calls this a major catalyst for wind, solar and storage PPAs and says the US Power Up basket (GSENEPOW) has P/E at 1y lows, RSI at 50 and lackluster price performance, and the author says 'I think its a buy'.

tension_points.bull_case: Le Pen's proposals point to sharp deficit reduction (3.7% of economic output in 2027, 2.2% by 2032). OAT-Bund spreads are about 10bps tighter and French domestic stocks and banks are up about 2 standard deviations from oversold levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Details from the far-right's budget are still to come, budget discussions and election noise could limit the government's ability to show tangible consolidation, and Le Pen might have less influence than needed to implement it.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Risk asymmetry turning negative again if lingering budget discussions and further election noise keep the market unconvinced of tangible fiscal consolidation.
